Can Intuitive Surgical Stock Hit $700?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) stock would have to rise another 49% from its November 5, 2026 close to reach $700. The maker of da Vinci systems would mainly need continued revenue growth to hit that mark, following a 20.5% increase over the twelve months to September 2026. After a 23.7% gain over the past three months, how much could three more years of owning the shares still make you?

A Trefis scenario built on Intuitive’s own figures values the shares at about $835 three years from now, placing the stock above $700 and 78.2% above the November 5 close. The table below compares the company today against that three-year projection.

Higher revenue accounts for most of that gain, at 83.2%. The instruments and accessories surgeons use in each da Vinci procedure make up the largest part of the business, representing 59.8% of fiscal 2025 revenue.

The scenario also assumes a slightly higher P/E in year three. Because today’s multiple sits well below the stock’s 66.1 average at fiscal quarter-ends over the past three years, the model moves the P/E 40% of the way toward that mark.

Sales outgrew procedures in the third quarter of 2026, when revenue rose 22% and total procedures grew 15%. Management said the difference reflects growth in system placements, alongside a richer product mix as da Vinci 5, its single-port SP system and Ion become a larger part of the business. The company placed 546 da Vinci systems in the quarter, up from 427 a year earlier.

Management is also cutting some instrument prices. The company expects pricing actions in high-volume benign procedures, such as hernia repair, alongside a price reduction in China that begins in November, to lower da Vinci instrument and accessory revenue per procedure by about 3% to 5% once fully in place. Management said the shift toward da Vinci 5 and SP is left out of that estimate and will add to revenue per procedure. Those price cuts work against sales outgrowing procedures, while the product shift works in favor of it. Management’s 2026 outlook holds no revenue forecast, but expects da Vinci procedure growth of 14% to 15% for a year with three quarters already reported.

Intuitive Surgical stock weighs strong growth against legal charge
sum: Intuitive Surgical reported strong operating growth for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, but a proposed antitrust settlement weighed heavily on reported earnings. The company disclosed the results and legal agreement on October 20 in a SEC filing.

Revenue increased 22 percent to 3.05 billion US dollars from 2.51 billion US dollars a year earlier. The main recurring revenue stream, instruments and accessories, grew 18 percent to 1.80 billion US dollars. Systems revenue rose to 769 million US dollars from 590 million US dollars as placements increased.

Worldwide procedures across the da Vinci and Ion platforms grew approximately 15 percent year over year. Da Vinci procedures increased approximately 14 percent, while Ion procedures advanced approximately 31 percent. Intuitive placed 546 da Vinci systems, compared with 427 in the prior-year quarter, including 315 da Vinci 5 systems against 240 a year earlier.

The installed base also expanded. Da Vinci systems reached 12,094 at September 30, up 12 percent from 10,763 a year earlier. The Ion installed base rose 21 percent to 1,152 systems. Intuitive said customers performed more than 10,000 procedures per day on average during the quarter.

GAAP net income attributable to Intuitive Surgical fell to 523 million US dollars, or 1.49 US dollars per diluted share, from 704 million US dollars, or 1.95 US dollars per share, in the third quarter of 2025. The result included a 450 million US-dollar pre-tax charge tied to a proposed settlement of previously disclosed antitrust class-action litigation.

The agreement covers claims concerning servicing of da Vinci systems and EndoWrist instruments. Intuitive said it made no admission of liability or wrongdoing. The settlement remains subject to preliminary and final court approval, so its final legal and financial status is not yet settled.

On a non-GAAP basis, which excludes the litigation charge and other specified items, net income rose to 1.05 billion US dollars, or 3.00 US dollars per diluted share, from 867 million US dollars, or 2.40 US dollars per share. The contrast highlights the difference between the company's underlying operating momentum and the one-time legal burden.

sum: Intuitive Surgical reported strong third-quarter growth on October 20, 2026, but a proposed antitrust settlement weighed heavily on GAAP earnings. In its earnings release, the surgical-robotics company said revenue increased 22% year over year to USD 3.05 billion for the quarter ended September 30.

Worldwide procedures across the da Vinci and Ion platforms increased 15% from the year-earlier quarter. Da Vinci procedures rose 14%, while Ion procedures advanced 31%. Instruments and accessories revenue grew 18% to USD 1.80 billion, supported by higher procedure volumes and the expanding installed base.

Intuitive placed 546 da Vinci systems during the quarter, up from 427 a year earlier. The placements included 315 da Vinci 5 systems, compared with 240 in the prior-year period. The da Vinci installed base reached 12,094 systems at September 30, up 12% year over year, while the Ion installed base rose 21% to 1,152 systems.

The company recorded a USD 450 million pre-tax charge related to an agreement to settle previously disclosed antitrust class-action litigation. The proposed settlement includes a one-time payment and injunctive relief, but remains subject to preliminary and final court approval. Intuitive said the agreement was reached without an admission of liability or wrongdoing.

The charge reduced third-quarter GAAP net income attributable to Intuitive Surgical to USD 523 million, or USD 1.49 per diluted share, from USD 704 million, or USD 1.95 per share, a year earlier. The expense amounted to USD 347 million after tax, or USD 0.99 per diluted share. On a non-GAAP basis, which excludes litigation charges and other specified items, net income rose to USD 1.05 billion from USD 867 million, while diluted earnings increased to USD 3.00 from USD 2.40.

Intuitive also recorded a USD 22 million after-tax benefit from refunds for tariffs paid in prior periods. The company repurchased 7.8 million shares for USD 2.94 billion during the quarter, leaving cash, cash equivalents and investments at USD 6.80 billion at September 30.
Management kept its full-year 2026 outlook for worldwide da Vinci procedure growth at 14% to 15% and expects the result to land closer to the midpoint.

Intuitive Surgical Stock Just Fell Despite a 22% Revenue Jump. Here's What Investors Are Missing.
sum: Shares of Intuitive Surgical (NASDAQ: ISRG) fell after the surgical robotics company reported earnings on Oct. 20. That drop came despite a 22% revenue jump. The real story that investors are missing is that sales of the da Vinci surgical robot aren't the main driver of the company's revenue. Here's what is.

The big concern about surgical robotics right now is that competition is heating up. Medtronic (NYSE: MDT) and Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) have each entered the fray. Both are well-respected medical device makers, so they are likely to gain traction with devices that compete against Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci system. Investors appear to view this as a material threat to Intuitive Surgical's growth prospects.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

It is, but there's ample room for growth even with new entrants. Notably, Intuitive Surgical sold more da Vinci systems in the third quarter of 2026 than it did in the same quarter of 2025. So, despite new players, growth hasn't stopped. And, notably, the number of procedures using a da Vinci system rose by 15%, while the number of installed systems increased by "only" 12% year over year.

The fact that procedures are increasing faster than robot sales is important to understand, because it highlights the demand for robotic surgery. It also leans into one of Intuitive Surgical's largest strengths. The sale of robots accounts for roughly 25% of revenues, while the sale of instruments, accessories, and services makes up the rest of the top line. So while selling da Vinci systems is important, the real business driver is what amounts to parts and services.

To be fair, Intuitive Surgical's stock price has recovered from the earnings-related drop, and then some. But that drop highlights an ongoing perception issue. While new competition will likely be a business headwind, Intuitive Surgical's already large installed base of over 12,000 systems has created an annuity-like cash flow machine to support the company's business.

Intuitive Surgical experienced notable upward momentum driven primarily by positive sentiment around international platform expansion and clinical milestones. Recent regulatory progress in Europe, including milestone CE mark approvals for expanded da Vinci single-port gynecologic indications and advances in flagship platform applications for cardiac procedures, reinforced confidence in the company's expanding total addressable market. These regulatory clearances highlight Intuitive's ongoing technological differentiation and continuous clinical widening of its robotic platforms, offsetting recent regional growth concerns.

The positive price movement also reflects institutional buying following a prolonged valuation compression in prior months. Concerns over moderated U.S. procedure growth, GLP-1 headwinds in bariatrics, and foreign tender delays had created an oversold technical setup. Institutional portfolio managers appear to be accumulating shares at perceived value levels, supported by the business model's high proportion of recurring revenue from instruments, accessories, and system servicing. The growth trajectory of the Ion endoluminal platform further underscores long-term operational resilience.

Additionally, investor positioning ahead of the upcoming third-quarter earnings report contributed to intraday volatility and upward price action. Wall Street maintains an overwhelmingly constructive consensus outlook on the stock, expecting procedure volume expansion and system placements to validate long-term growth forecasts. While near-term headwinds such as capital expenditure discipline at hospitals and international pricing pressures remain points of debate, positive product developments and strategic execution continue to support market sentiment.

This suggests that product cost reductions and operating leverage are increasingly offsetting higher freight and semiconductor-memory costs, as well as the favorable margin impact of faster growth in newer platforms.

sum: Intuitive Surgical Inc. (NASDAQ:ISRG) shares fell sharply after the medical technology company released second-quarter results that topped Wall Street forecasts but issued a full-year procedure growth outlook that failed to meet investor expectations.

The robotic surgery specialist reported adjusted earnings of $2.80 per share for the quarter, exceeding analyst estimates of $2.51 by $0.29. Revenue increased 19% year over year to $2.89 billion from $2.44 billion in the second quarter of 2025, also ahead of the consensus forecast of $2.82 billion.
Quarterly results included an after-tax benefit of $28 million, equal to $0.08 per share, related to refunds of tariffs paid in previous periods.

Despite delivering stronger-than-expected quarterly financial results, Intuitive Surgical's shares dropped 10.9% after management projected full-year 2026 da Vinci procedure growth of between 13.5% and 15.5%, with performance expected to land around the midpoint of 14.5%.

The company also forecast an adjusted gross profit margin of 68.0% to 69.0% of revenue, including an estimated one percentage point impact from tariffs. Adjusted operating expenses are expected to increase between 11% and 13% during the year.
Combined worldwide procedures across the company's da Vinci and Ion platforms increased approximately 16% during the second quarter.
Da Vinci procedures rose roughly 15%, while Ion procedures climbed approximately 36%.

Intuitive Surgical’s Stock Has Fallen Over 25% This Year, but Goldman Sachs Still Recommends Investors Buy
sum: Over the past 12 months, Intuitive Surgical, Inc. (ISRG) has faced numerous challenges, with its stock price declining 26% cumulatively. However, some Wall Street analysts remain optimistic about the stock, and the target prices set by multiple analysts suggest considerable upside from current levels. David Roman, an analyst at Goldman Sachs (GS), is among them. He recently maintained a “Buy” rating on the stock and set a 12-month target price of $558, which is 47% above Intuitive Surgical’s current share price.

The recent headwinds facing Intuitive Surgical include lower-than-expected profit margins related to the “Da Vinci 5,” the latest version of the da Vinci surgical robot system launched in 2024. The system has seen strong market acceptance, but its profit margins are lower than those of its predecessor. In addition, this medical device specialist is also grappling with rising costs stemming from high tariffs. It remains unclear whether the company can resolve these challenges within the next 6 to 12 months.

Nevertheless, there are solid reasons to be optimistic about Intuitive Surgical’s long-term prospects. Take the Da Vinci 5, for example. This new product offers multiple advantages over its predecessor, among which force feedback technology allows surgeons to perceive tissue pressure and texture through the robotic manipulator, providing better tactile sensation and helping to make delicate surgeries safer, more precise, and easier to perform. With these enhanced features, the Da Vinci 5 is expected to attract surgeons or hospitals that were previously hesitant to use the da Vinci system, thereby helping the company expand its market and potentially gain indications that previous generations could not obtain. This would lead to a larger installed base, as well as stronger and more profitable recurring revenue from instruments and accessories.

Intuitive Surgical still has a substantial addressable market in the robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) industry. Robotic-assisted surgery enables surgeons to perform minimally invasive procedures that offer significant advantages over open surgery, yet market penetration remains insufficient, and with the global population aging, the market is expected to grow further.
